claims.text: An HEA contains at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
The proposed starting material is a fully disordered, single-phase solid solution outside the well-studied Nb-Ta and titanium-rich families.
The superconducting transition temperature of the target HEA is predominantly governed by its average valence electron concentration.
Changing VEC changes electronic band filling.
Changing VEC modulates the density of states at the Fermi level.
The degree of compositional disorder influences the density of states at the Fermi level.
The density of states at the Fermi level affects the strength of electron-phonon coupling.
Electron-phonon coupling supports Cooper pairing in superconducting HEAs.
Moderate disorder-induced electron scattering can beneficially tune electron-phonon coupling by smoothing electronic states.
Excessive disorder enhances electron scattering and eventually suppresses superconductivity.
There is an optimal VEC or band filling at which Tc is maximized.
Compositional substitutions toward the optimal VEC will increase Tc relative to the unmodified alloy.
Compositional substitutions to VEC values above or below the optimum will lower Tc relative to the baseline.
Microstructural defects may independently modify Tc.
The proposed VEC mechanism applies only while the alloy remains a single-phase, fully disordered solid solution and all constituent concentrations remain at least 5 atomic percent.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is declared applicable only when secondary phases are absent, but the falsification rule treats correlation of Tc with emerging secondary phases as falsifying the hypothesis. Secondary-phase formation instead places those samples outside the stated applicability domain and is therefore a confound or boundary violation rather than a decisive falsifier.
